witnesses.evidence_phrase: And Michael, and Gabriel, and Raphael, and Phanuel shall take hold of them on that great day, and cast them on that day into the burning furnace, that the Lord of Spirits may take vengeance on them for their unrighteousness in becoming subject to Satan and leading astray those who dwell on the earth.
witnesses.rationale: This passage independently preserves the second-temple tradition that a body of angelic beings rebelled by becoming subject to Satan and leading humanity astray, and that they face judicial confinement and fiery vengeance. It runs parallel to the New Testament pattern in 2 Peter 2:4, Jude 6, and Matthew 25:41 of angels who sinned and are kept for judgment in fire. It is a parallel rather than a direct dependence: the lexical verdict rests on the canonical texts, and 1 Enoch is the shared milieu they drew on, not their source of authority.

witnesses.evidence_phrase: For I saw all the angels of punishment abiding (there) and preparing all the instruments of Satan.
witnesses.rationale: This verse names a class of angels associated with Satan and the apparatus of his work, reinforcing the second-temple picture of a satanic order operating among the angelic ranks. It parallels the canonical pairing of the devil with his angels in Matthew 25:41 and the dragon and his angels in Revelation 12:7 to 9. It attests the shared milieu rather than supplying the verdict, so the attestation type is parallel.

witnesses.evidence_phrase: their ruin is accomplished because they have learnt all the secrets of the angels, and all the violence of the Satans, and all their powers
witnesses.rationale: This passage attributes secret knowledge, violence, and corrupting powers to a plurality of angelic and satanic agents, matching the Watchers tradition in which rebel angels taught forbidden arts to humanity. It parallels the New Testament view of hostile spiritual powers in Ephesians 6:12 and of angels who abandoned their proper station in Jude 6. It corroborates the surrounding milieu, not the verdict, so the attestation type is parallel.

witnesses.rationale: Philo cites the psalm phrase evil angels and identifies a class of angelic beings characterized by wickedness, supplying a roughly contemporary Jewish witness to the category of malign angels. His allegorical reading recasts the figures morally rather than narrating a literal rebellion, so it preserves the same broad tradition in parallel rather than directly corroborating the rebellion-and-confinement schema of 2 Peter 2:4 and Jude 6. The verdict rests on the canonical texts; Philo attests the surrounding vocabulary.

summary: The extra-biblical record gives a clear second-temple background for the proposition that a portion of the angels fell into rebellion and now oppose God. The strongest witness is 1 Enoch, whose Watchers and Parables traditions repeatedly describe angelic beings who become subject to Satan, lead humanity astray, wield violent and corrupting powers, and are reserved for fiery judgment under named archangels. These passages run parallel to the canonical pattern in 2 Peter 2:4, Jude 6, Matthew 25:41, and Revelation 12:7 to 9, where angels who sinned are kept in confinement for judgment and the devil is paired with his angels. Philo of Alexandria adds a roughly contemporary Jewish voice that knows the category of evil angels, though he reads it allegorically as moral wickedness rather than narrating a literal angelic revolt. None of these witnesses establishes the doctrine, which rests on the canonical texts named in the lexical verdict. They attest the shared milieu in which that doctrine was articulated, so each is recorded as a parallel rather than independent corroboration. Reading Jude or 2 Peter as simple borrowings from 1 Enoch would overstate the dependence, so the relationship is treated as composite tradition. The remaining candidate chunks, including Josephus on storms and law, Philo on the tower of Babel, the Roman witnesses on Christians, the Mishnah tractates, and the Qumran divine-name fragments, do not materially address fallen or rebel angels and were not cited.
